handoff.purpose: Implement refresh, gate-mode check, drift description, text renderer, and CLI entry point.

symbols.name: refresh
symbols.note: Builds inventory doc and writes it to target; returns path, doc, and harvest stats.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Gate mode: verifies inventory existence, parseability, schema, digest, annotation overreach, and freshness; returns problems list.

symbols.name: _by_key
symbols.note: Extracts derived fields of each feature keyed by module or detector:reason, dropping human fields.

symbols.name: _statuses
symbols.note: Returns map of feature key to status string.

symbols.name: _describe_drift
symbols.note: Compares stored vs fresh inventory and produces human-readable drift messages (head, statuses, blocks, feature fields).

symbols.name: render_text
symbols.note: Formats inventory doc as a short human-readable text summary.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: parses args, dispatches to check, json output, or refresh.

claims.text: Gate mode. Writes nothing; returns {"ok": bool, "problems": [...]}.
claims.why: The function never calls write_inventory or any write; it only reads and returns a dict with 'ok' and 'problems'.

claims.text: Four ways to fail, in the order a reader needs them: 1. there is no inventory, or it cannot be parsed; 2. it was written by a different schema; 3. its digest does not cover its own derived fields -- somebody edited the mechanical half by hand; 4. regenerating it now would change something -- it is STALE, and the diff says exactly how.
claims.why: The code checks stored None (line 855), __error__ (line 858), schema mismatch (line 861), digest_ok (line 864), annotation_overreach (line 868), and then compares fresh build (line 874-876) to detect staleness.

claims.text: Every feature's DERIVED half, keyed by module (or by detector for the module-less stale entries). The human fields are dropped so a note cannot read as drift.
claims.why: The function iterates areas/features, constructs key as module or 'detector:reason', and filters out FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS.

claims.text: A module whose importers or reaching entry point changed is a real difference, and reporting it as "something differs, go diff the file yourself" is how a gate stops being read.
claims.why: The code includes field-level comparison beyond status in the 'moved' list (lines 940-948).

claims.text: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run; human notes are carried forward and excluded from the digest.
claims.why: This chunk defines refresh and build but the actual carrying-forward and digest exclusion logic is in build and harvest, not visible here. The claim is plausible but cannot be fully verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: gate mode: exit non-zero if the file is missing, hand-edited or stale; writes nothing
claims.why: In main, args.check calls check() and returns 1 if problems exist; no writes occur in that branch (lines 977-984).

claims.text: print the generated document; writes nothing
claims.why: The --json branch builds a doc and prints it; no write_inventory call (lines 986-993).
probe = not args.no_git (line 977) and probe is passed to check and refresh as probe_dirty.
If neither --refresh, --check, nor --json is given, ap.error is called with that message.

claims.text: Regenerate with `python -m daedalus.mapping.inventory --refresh` (or `daedalus map`, which does it as part of the run).
claims.where: main print in check failure branch (line 982)
claims.why: The claim about 'daedalus map' is outside this chunk; the --refresh command is valid per this chunk.

observations.what: check() returns 'stored' and 'fresh' in the result dict even when ok is true; callers may use them.
The --json branch in main does not pass reports to build; it calls analyse_once and then build again, duplicating work.
refresh() does not handle the case where target is a directory; write_inventory may fail.
_describe_drift compares top-level blocks (env_vars, cli_commands, etc.) with simple equality, which may miss drift if the blocks are reordered but semantically equal.
